rules.name: Low arch + arch discomfort + inner wear
rules.say: Your arch sits lower, and the wear on your current shoe backs that up. A shoe with a firmer platform under the arch usually feels steadier late in the day.
rules.report: Your fitting showed a lower arch with some inward wear. We recommended a supportive shoe and an arch-support insole for added comfort.

rules.name: Low arch, no discomfort
rules.say: No complaints today — we'll keep a little structure under the arch so it stays that way, without over-correcting anything.
rules.report: A lower arch with no current discomfort. We suggested a shoe with light built-in support.
rules.guard: Do not manufacture a problem. Comfort framing only.

rules.name: High arch + impact discomfort
rules.say: Higher arches tend to spread impact across less of the foot, so cushioning does more work for you than structure does.
rules.report: Your fitting showed a higher arch. We recommended a neutral, well-cushioned shoe with a flexible feel.

rules.name: High arch + outer-edge wear
rules.say: Your weight is riding along the outside edge. Extra stability posts would push you further that way — cushioning and a well-shaped heel are the better answer.
rules.report: Your wear pattern showed more contact along the outer edge. We recommended a cushioned, neutral shoe.

rules.name: Strong inward roll + knee or ankle discomfort
rules.say: There's a noticeable inward roll. A stability shoe gives that a firmer base — and if the knee keeps bothering you, that's worth a conversation with a professional.
rules.report: We fitted you in a shoe with added support based on how your foot loads. Comfort should be your guide as you break it in.
rules.guard: No causal claim between shoe and knee.

rules.name: Heel discomfort + 8+ hours standing
rules.say: Eight-plus hours is a lot of load on the heel. We want cushioning that lasts the shift and a heel that holds you steady, not just soft foam that bottoms out by two o'clock.
rules.report: Long hours on your feet with heel discomfort. We recommended a cushioned, supportive shoe and a heel-comfort insole.

rules.name: Heel discomfort worst on first steps
rules.say: That first-thing-in-the-morning pattern is common. Structured heel support and arch support tend to feel better through the day — and since it's been ongoing, it's worth mentioning to a healthcare professional.
rules.report: You mentioned heel discomfort in the morning. We recommended a supportive shoe with a structured heel and an arch-support insole for comfort.

rules.name: Forefoot discomfort + wide foot
rules.say: The ball of your foot needs room to spread out — a wider toe box plus cushioning right under that area takes the pressure off.
rules.report: Your fitting showed a wider forefoot with discomfort at the ball of the foot. We recommended a wider toe box and forefoot cushioning.

rules.name: Toe discomfort + tight current shoe
rules.say: Let's check length and width before anything else — a lot of toe discomfort is simply half a size or one width away. You want about a thumb's width in front of the longest toe.
rules.report: Your current shoes were fitting tight through the toes. We checked sizing and recommended a roomier toe box.

rules.name: Ankle instability
rules.say: A firmer heel counter — this back part here — makes a real difference in how steady a shoe feels. Squeeze it and you'll feel the difference between these two.
rules.report: We recommended a shoe with a structured heel for a more secure, stable feel.

rules.name: Knee, hip or back discomfort + active
rules.say: More shock absorption is a reasonable thing to try. I'd also rotate between two pairs if you're out most days. If it persists, it's worth having someone take a proper look.
rules.report: We focused on shock absorption and support for your activity level.
rules.guard: No claim that footwear resolves knee, hip or back discomfort.

rules.name: Blisters or rubbing
rules.say: Rubbing is almost always movement — either the shoe is a touch long, or the heel isn't locked in. Let me show you a heel-lock lacing that fixes most of it.
rules.report: We checked fit and lacing to reduce movement inside the shoe.

rules.name: Wide foot in a narrow current model
rules.say: You've been in a narrow last. Same size, wider fit — you'll feel the difference immediately, and it isn't about going up a size.
rules.report: We recommended a wider fit rather than a longer shoe.

rules.name: Orthotic user + volume
rules.say: Bring your orthotic — we fit the shoe to it. That means the factory insole has to come out, and sometimes a half size up to make room.
rules.report: We fitted your shoes to work with your existing orthotics, using a removable-insole design.
rules.guard: Never recommend a competing insole. Never modify or comment on a custom orthotic.

rules.name: Low volume foot + heel slip
rules.say: Your foot doesn't fill the shoe vertically, which is why the heel lifts. A narrower heel or a lacing change usually solves it without going down a size.
rules.report: We chose a shoe with a more secure heel fit for your foot volume.

rules.name: Size asymmetry
rules.say: Your feet are slightly different sizes — that's completely normal. We fit the larger one and take up the extra space on the other side.
rules.report: Your feet measured slightly different sizes. We fitted the larger foot for comfort.

rules.name: Bunion or toe accommodation
rules.say: We want a rounder, softer toe box with no seam sitting right on that spot. Let me check where this shoe's stitching lands on your foot.
rules.report: We recommended a rounder, roomier toe box with a soft upper for comfort.
rules.guard: Accommodation language only. Never suggest a shoe corrects a toe position.

rules.name: Heel slip at standard width
rules.say: Before we change size, try this lacing — it locks the heel down. If it still lifts, we'll look at a shoe with a narrower heel.
rules.report: We adjusted lacing and heel fit to keep your foot secure in the shoe.

rules.name: Runner + knee discomfort + uneven wear
rules.say: Your wear pattern isn't even, which is worth paying attention to as a runner. A stability shoe is a sensible next step, and when our gait platform is in we can look at this properly.
rules.report: Based on your running and your shoe wear pattern, we recommended a stability running shoe.
rules.guard: No injury-prevention claim. Never promise a hardware date.

rules.name: Neutral runner + high mileage
rules.say: At your mileage, foam compresses faster than most people expect. Two pairs in rotation usually last longer than two pairs run back to back.
rules.report: We recommended a neutral, cushioned running shoe suited to your mileage.

rules.name: Work + 8+ hours standing
rules.say: For a full shift, durability and an anti-fatigue insole matter as much as the shoe. The insole is the cheapest upgrade to how your legs feel at hour eight.
rules.report: Long shifts on hard surfaces. We recommended a durable, supportive work shoe with an anti-fatigue insole.

rules.name: Walking primary + comfort priority
rules.say: For walking, a smooth heel-to-toe roll is what you'll notice most. Take a lap on the hard floor, not the carpet — carpet flatters everything.
rules.report: We recommended a cushioned walking shoe with a smooth, comfortable stride.

rules.name: Hiking + ankle concern
rules.say: A mid-cut with a firm heel will feel more planted on uneven ground. Wear them around the house for a week before a long day out.
rules.report: We recommended a supportive hiking shoe with a structured heel, plus break-in time before longer hikes.
rules.guard: No claim about preventing ankle injury.

rules.name: Kids fitting
rules.say: We want about a thumb's width of growing room — enough to last, not so much they trip. I'd re-check the size in about three months.
rules.report: We fitted with growing room and recommended re-checking size in about three months.
rules.guard: SUPPRESS_UPSELL: no insole or orthotic upsell to minors.

rules.name: Previous return: too narrow
rules.say: Last time the width was the issue, so let's start a width up rather than a size up — that's usually the fix.
rules.report: We adjusted width based on your previous experience.

rules.name: Previous return: uncomfortable
rules.say: Since the last pair didn't work out, let's take a bit longer. Walk both of these and tell me what you notice — I'd rather get it right than fast.
rules.report: We took extra time on fit and will check in with you shortly after purchase.
rules.guard: Follow-up forced to 7 days. This rule intentionally costs time.

rules.name: Current shoe 2+ years old
rules.say: Foam compresses over time, so a new pair will feel firmer at first even at the same model and size. That's the cushioning working, not the shoe being wrong.
rules.report: Your previous shoes were well used. New footwear may feel firmer at first — that's normal.

rules.name: Custom orthotic user
rules.say: We build the fit around your orthotic. The stock insole comes out, and we check depth so your foot isn't sitting too high in the shoe.
rules.report: We selected footwear compatible with your custom orthotics.
rules.guard: SUPPRESS_UPSELL: never sell against a custom orthotic.

rules.name: Price priority + support need
rules.say: If budget's the constraint, a solid shoe plus a good insole often beats a pricier shoe on its own — and the insole moves to your next pair.
rules.report: We balanced support and budget, including an insole option that carries over to future footwear.

rules.name: Red-flag routing
rules.say: Let's keep this simple and comfortable — roomy, soft, nothing pressing anywhere. Given what you've described, it's worth having a healthcare professional take a look too.
rules.report: We focused on a roomy, low-pressure fit for your comfort.
rules.guard: SUPPRESS_UPSELL: highest-sensitivity rule. No diagnosis, no alarm, no product claim.
